the question is how far FleXray's renders are from real X-rays of both kinds, plain film and intra-operative fluoroscopy, and whether that distance passes the distance between two real corpora (PREREG.md section 1), so every held corpus of the two kinds is a group, the real-against-real pairs giving the scale, and the render groups share their CTs so that each pair of them isolates one part of the recipe (README section 2.2); the owner asked on 2026-10-25 for every held corpus, plain film and fluoroscopy both (README, opening)

a map alone answers neither question, since t-SNE draws clusters for any two sets with a consistent difference, however small, and its distances between clusters mean nothing (README section 1); so every claim is carried by a test with an interval and a calibration, a classifier two-sample test, which learns to tell the two sets apart, among them, beside a kernel test and distances that learn nothing (PREREG.md section 3); the owner asked on 2026-10-25 for the statistical tests for separation that machine learning experts would do (README, opening)

items.asks: All transforms, from raw data to the model's input
items.evidence: every image, synthetic or real, decoded to floats (DICOM through its modality LUT, MONOCHROME1 turned bone-bright, a cine's middle frame), windowed to its own 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles, cut to the centre square of 0.9 of its shorter side and resized to 256 by area; each feature space reads the mean of its features of the image and of its inverse, and FleXray's space also the image as stored (tools/domain_gap.py at commit 6e908e6, README section 3)

no network is trained; the models fit are the two-sample classifiers, logistic regression and 15 nearest neighbours, in each fold of every contrast, every contrast kept in results.json on the grid and 35 of them in summary.txt's lines; units 768 of 768 done, 0 failed (summary.txt record)

README section 1 gives each test's reason: the classifier two-sample test, scored out of fold with every person wholly on one side of each split, with a person-cluster bootstrap interval and a person-level permutation p; the MMD, a kernel test with a person-level permutation p; the Frechet distance and KID in each space's first 64 components, so that every space is compared at one dimension and with a stable covariance; precision, recall, density and coverage, which say whether the renders lie inside the real manifold and how much of it they cover, the two ways a renderer can fail; and three feature spaces, so that no finding rests on one encoder's view (README section 3); the classifiers are logistic regression and 15 nearest neighbours (PREREG.md section 3)

every two-sample test scored out of fold over at most five folds grouped by person and stratified by label, so a person is wholly on one side of each split; the split-half nulls split each group of at least 40 persons in two by person; every draw from seed 0 (summary.txt record; tools/domain_gap.py at commit 6e908e6, README sections 1 and 4)

the baselines are the real-against-real contrasts, every pair of real groups and pooled fluoroscopy against pooled film, the median AUC and median FD64 of a family's own real pairs being what each primary word and gap ratio is read against (PREREG.md sections 3 and 4), and the split-half nulls, where every test must find nothing (CLAIM 32 quotes them); summary.txt carries such lines in the spaces flexray, imagenet

items.asks: Preprocessing fit on training data only
items.evidence: every classifier fits its scaler and PCA inside its own pipeline on the rows it is trained on: the C2ST's in each fold on the folds that hold none of the scored rows' persons, the real-group classifier's accuracy out of fold the same way, and the classifier that calls each synthetic group on the real rows alone (tools/domain_gap_stats.py, classifier, c2st, real_group_accuracy and nearest_real), so no row shapes its own score; each image is windowed by its own percentiles, so decoding fits nothing across images (README section 3); the standardised features and first 64 components that the MMD, FD64, KID64, PRDC and the structure measures read are fit on every row of the reading without its labels, so they are the same under every permutation of a test's labels (tools/domain_gap.py at commit 6e908e6, space_head)

by person: every test's folds are grouped by person, so no person is on both sides of a split, and two render groups on one CT folder are read as a paired sample whose two views of a CT fall in one fold (tools/domain_gap.py at commit 6e908e6); in the 7 groups whose persons are their files (summary.txt, persons by file: fluorogen, aasce, nhanes2, csxa, kub_stonex, ieee_lateral, aariz) only files are held apart

every feature is computed from one image's pixels alone, by the encoders and the physics measures (PREREG.md section 3), and the steps before them take away what would tell corpora apart by their files rather than their images: each image is cut to its centre square, so no pad's flat border marks a corpus of non-square images, resized to 256 alike and windowed to its own percentiles, and the primary reading is invariant to inversion, so polarity alone separates nothing in it (README section 3); what still tells corpora apart besides realism, their anatomy, devices, eras and formats, was listed before the run in README section 5

items.asks: Uncertainty and how it was computed
items.evidence: summary.txt: 35 AUCs with an interval, 34 with a C2ST permutation p, 34 MMD permutation p and 6 Benjamini-Hochberg q; each interval the 95 percent percentile interval of a person-cluster bootstrap of 1,000 draws, the C2ST's p from 100 permutations and the MMD's from 1,000, all by person, and the q by Benjamini-Hochberg within a space, the MMD's over its contrasts and its split-half nulls as PREREG.md section 3 says, the worded pairs' q over the contrasts alone on their verdict lines (DEVIATIONS.md, item 11) (tools/domain_gap.py at commit 6e908e6 and tools/domain_gap_stats.py, README section 4)

the C2ST's 100 permutations, run against each family and in the replication pairs, and the MMD's 1,000 shuffle the labels by person, every row of a person moving together, and a CT's rows on both sides together where both sides render the same CTs, so each p holds under the null that persons are exchangeable between the two sets; the AUC's 95 percent interval is a person-cluster bootstrap that holds each fold's trained classifiers fixed, so it is narrow for a few dozen persons, which is why a split-half null is flagged by its MMD and not by its interval (DEVIATIONS.md, item 8); Benjamini-Hochberg runs over a space's MMD p-values and over its C2ST permutation p-values (PREREG.md section 3; CLAIM 29 says which family this run's MMD q took) and controls the false-discovery rate where the p-values are independent or positively dependent, while a space's contrasts share groups and so are not independent
